_capture.method: fetched with the Arena fetch tool (the development sandbox has no outbound network; CI does)
_capture.completeness: Complete response body as returned by the fetch tool: 2 finalized KXNHLOVERTIME contracts plus the paging cursor (2026 Stanley Cup Final games 5 and 6). Transcribed at capture time; no value was edited.
_capture.why_it_matters: Proves the overtime market exists with a historical tier and real volume (19,512.97 and 39,558.66 contracts), that its contracts carry NO floor_strike and NO strike_type (it is strike-less, unlike totals and spreads), and that the rules text is 'If <A> and <B> go to overtime ... resolves to Yes'. It also shows why the definition must be verified rather than assumed: both of these games are playoff games, where a shootout is impossible, so this pair says nothing about whether a regular-season game decided in a shootout settles YES. That question is answered empirically by verify.py against the NHL's own lastPeriodType instead of by assumption.
